page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific multi-threaded and memory-intensive tasks. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 269.5 GB/sec and large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 209.21 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and extended instruction tests also rank in the top 25% of tested servers. Conversely, the platform exhibits average performance in standard single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, and shows relative weakness in large language model text generation, where the medium 7B model yields 8.69 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.16xlarge provides high compute density with dedicated CPU allocation, making it suitable for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are externalized to network volumes. This profile is suited for database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, parallel compilation, and static web serving, while being less optimal for large-scale LLM text generation or memory-heavy caching layers.
